# read_A: p. 107 ll. 3–5, pp. 108, 109 (images n108, n109, n110), read from the images

## Lines and layout

- p. 107 (n108): five lines; I read 107.3–107.5 (107.1–2 belong to part 011). Skew +1.9°, read from a straightened copy. Headlines at about 132, 186, 246, 300, 350.
- p. 108 (n109): five lines. Leaf back, no ornament. Skew −2.0°, straightened. Headlines at about 126, 176, 230, 284, 336.
- p. 109 (n110): five lines. Leaf front, opens with the swirl, `༔`, a wide blank, `༔`: written `༄༅༔ ༔`. Skew +0.9°, straightened. Line 109.5 ends at about two thirds of the line (`…ལྷོ་ནས་རྡོ་རྗེ་སེར་མོ`), and the rest of the line is filler dots up to the frame. The first dot is at headline height right after `མོ` and is taken as its tsheg; the rest are left out.
- In all, 13 print lines in read_A.txt.

**Seam with part 011 (start).** 107.2 ends `…དེ་ལ་མ་འཇིགས་ཤིག༔`; 107.3 begins `ཀྱཻ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ལྷོ་ནས…`. Clean.
**Seam with B.** 109.5 ends `…ལྷོ་ནས་རྡོ་རྗེ་སེར་མོ་` + filler dots; p. 110 should start with the southern gatekeeper's head (other recension `ར་མགོ་མ`).

## Method

- Skew per image found by maximising the variance of the row profile; all reading done on rotated copies (bicubic).
- Line bands from the row profile; each line cropped in four or five overlapping segments at ×3 (LANCZOS); doubtful places at ×5–×12, some binarised and enlarged NEAREST, and side-by-side montages for letter shapes:
  the 107.3 head against ཞ of `ཞི་བ` (107.3), ད/ང of `པ་དང` (107.3), ཕ of `ཕག་མོ` / `ཕག་གི` (109.1), the letter of 107.5 `?འི་མགོ`, and པུ/ཤུ of `པུ་ཤུད` (108.3); and the 109.4 `སྒོ་མ་?་རྣལ་འབྱོར` against `བྱང་གི་རྣལ་འབྱོར` (109.3).
  For ཝ I also rendered the letter in the only Tibetan font on the machine (Unifont), enlarged, to have the shape of the letter beside the print.
- Mid-line tshegs are often fused to the head bars; where the image cannot decide I followed normal syllable division (as in 010/011).
- Line-end tshegs checked at ×7–×10.

## The 107.3 gap: now read `ཕ[?]་ཝད་མགོ`; and 107.5 `ཝའི` (C's སྤྲའི[?])

- **107.5 first.** C read the stack before `འི་མགོ` as ས over པ with ྲ. At ×8 it is **not a stack**: it has the height of one letter (top at the headline with ག and འ, bottom above ག's descender). Its shape: a curl at the top left hanging from the head bar, the bar, a middle horizontal, a closed loop at the bottom, and a right-hand descender. This is ཝ (the font form has exactly the top-left hook on a closed box). The other recension has `ཝའི་མགོ` (fox) here. **Written `ཝའི`, no [?]**; C's སྤྲའི[?] is withdrawn.
- **107.3.** After `སེར་མོ` come three letters before `མགོ`:
  1. A box-left letter with a diagonal and a right descender, with a small tick at the top right. The montage with ཕ of `ཕག་མོ` and `ཕག་གི` (109.1) matches; པ in this print has no tick. Read ཕ; marked [?] because the tick is small and could be a fused tsheg (then པ).
  2. **The same letter as 107.5's ཝ** (same top-left curl, middle bar, closed bottom loop, descender; side by side they are identical). Not ཞ (compared with `ཞི་བ` on the same line: ཞ has a large round left loop), not ཤ (ཤུ of `པུ་ཤུད` 108.3 is different and its ུ hangs below).
  3. ད, not ང: the bar, a short drop on the left, a short horizontal, then the diagonal, as in ད of `པ་དང`; ང of the same `དང` has a single diagonal from the bar.
  - Between 1 and 2 a dot at headline height, fused to the curl of ཝ: taken as the tsheg. So **`ཕ[?]་ཝད`**.
  - The other recension has `ཕག་མགོ་མ` (sow-headed); ཕག does not fit (no ག; letters 2–3 are clear). `ཕ་ཝད` is not a word I know; `ཕ་ཝང` "bat" differs by one letter (ད for ང). See misprints.

## [?] (2) and […] gaps (0)

| place | as written | candidates / why |
|---|---|---|
| 107.3 | `སེར་མོ་ཕ[?]་ཝད་མགོ` | ཕ or པ (see above). The ཝ and ད are clear. No gap any more. |
| 109.4 | `སྒོ་མ་རི[?]་རྣལ་འབྱོར་མ་བཞི` | After `སྒོ་མ` a letter with a gigu, then `རྣལ་འབྱོར` (matches `གི་རྣལ་འབྱོར` of 109.3 letter for letter in a montage). The letter under the gigu has a head bar, a diagonal and a left foot: ར (not ན, not ཡ). The other recension has `སྒོ་མ་རྣལ་འབྱོར་མ་བཞི` with nothing between. A stray `རི` makes no sense; perhaps `སྒོ་མ་རིགས་…`? or a dittography of the ར of རྣལ. Kept as read, note only. |

## Where the print differs from the other recension (print followed)

Spelling / wording only (same sense):
- 107.3, 108.1, 108.5, 109.4: `ཀྱཻ` (double e-sign), as before.
- 107.5 `དབྱུག་ཐོ` (also 108.3) for `དབྱུག་ཏོ`; 107.5 `ཐོགས་པ` for `ཕྱར་བ`.
- 108.1, 108.4, 109.3: `རང་གི་ཀླད་པའི`; `འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ` for `འཆར་རོ` / `ཡོང་ངོ`.
- 108.2/108.3 `ལག་ན` formula; 108.3 `སྤུ་གྲི་གཅོད་པ` for `སྤུ་གྲིས་གཅོད་པ` (no ས at ×8; the ྲ hook and ི of གྲི are clear).
- 108.4 `ནོར་སྲུང` for `ནོར་སྲུངས`; 108.4 `འགེངས` (ང and ས joined as one ligature, like the -གས ligature; written ངས).
- 108.5 `སྔོན་མོ`, 109.1 `སྐྱིན་གྱི་མགོ`, 109.2 `ཁྭ་ཏའི` as in the other recension.
- 109.2 `གླང་གི་མགོ` for `གླང་ཆེན་མགོ` (elephant/ox: `གླང` alone is "ox", `གླང་ཆེན` "elephant"; the goddess is སྣ་ཆེན "Big-nose", so elephant is meant; the print's wording is ambiguous, note only).
- 109.5 `ཁུ་བྱུག་མགོ` for `ཁུ་བྱུག་གི་མགོ་ཅན`.

Sense differences:

- **107.4** `ཟླ་བ་དམར་མོ` "red", other recension `དཀར་མོ` "white" (C saw the same).
- **107.5→108.1** `ལྷའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་|དྲུག` without `མ` (as C).

- **108.2** `སྟོབས་ཆེན་དམར་མོ` "red", other recension `དཀར་མོ` "white" (×5: ད, མ, ར clear).
- **108.3** `སྲིན་མོ་སེར་མོ` "yellow", other recension `དམར་མོ` "red" (×6).

- **108.4** `ནོར་སྲུང་ལྗང་ཁུ` "green", other recension `དམར་ལྗང` "red-green".

Note that the seventh northern goddess `ཆུ་ལྷ` is also snake-headed (109.3), so the print has two snake heads in the north; note only.

- **109.5** `ཤར་ནས་རྡོ་རྗེ་ཕག་མོ་ཁུ་བྱུག་མགོ` — **`ཕག་མོ`** where the other recension has `དཀར་མོ` (white). The ཕ matches `ཕག་མོ` of 109.1 in a montage (×7), and ག, མོ are clear. As it stands "Vajra-Sow, cuckoo-headed". Kept, note only (see misprints).

## Line-end tsheg status

- **With a tsheg:** 107.3 `ཐོགས་`; 107.4 `ཅོན་`; 107.5 `འབྱོར་` (against the frame); 108.1 `རྒོད་`; 108.4 `ནང་`; 108.5 `བ་`; 109.1 `ལག་`; 109.2 `བེ་`; 109.3 `རང་`; 109.4 `ནང་`; 109.5 `མོ་` (first of the filler dots).
- **Ending in ༔:** 108.2 `མགོ༔`.
- **No tsheg (fix below):** 108.3 `གཉིས` (×10: nothing at headline height before the frame).
- **Filler dots mid-line**, left out with the tsheg written: 108.4 `ནོར་…སྲུང`.
- **Mid-line missing tsheg:** 109.2 at the start of the line, `ནམཆེ` (×8: ན and མ touch at the head bar, no dot; the tsheg after ཆེ is clear).
- The 108.5/109.1 join crosses the ornament: `ལག་ན་བ་|༄༅༔ ༔དན་འཕྱར` — the tsheg is printed, no fix.

## Fixes needed (`# fix:` lines)

```
# fix: ལག་གཉིསམདའ་གཞུ => ལག་གཉིས་མདའ་གཞུ
# fix: ལག་ནམཆེ་ཞགས => ལག་ན་མཆེ་ཞགས
```

- No `པའཾ`, `ལཾ`, `ནམཁའ`, `འོངོ` contractions or subscript-ས forms on these lines. The `ངས` of 108.4 `འགེངས` is a joined ligature; written ངས (like the -གས ligature).

## Suspected misprints

1. **107.3 `ཕ[?]་ཝད་མགོ`.** No word ཕ་ཝད; `ཕ་ཝང` "bat" is one letter off (ད for ང) and is an animal. The other recension's `ཕག` (sow) cannot be read here. Moderate–low certainty for ཕ་ཝང. Proposed only if the editor wants it: `# fix: སེར་མོ་ཕ་ཝད་མགོ => སེར་མོ་ཕ་ཝང་མགོ` (rule 5b, note gives the print's reading); otherwise kept, note only ("an animal head, ཕ་ཝད as printed; perhaps for ཕ་ཝང bat").
2. **109.4 `སྒོ་མ་རི[?]་རྣལ་འབྱོར`.** A stray syllable; the sense allows only "the four gatekeeper yoginīs". Kept, note only (I cannot say what it was meant to be).
3. **109.5 `རྡོ་རྗེ་ཕག་མོ`** for the expected colour (`དཀར་མོ`). Probably the carver's eye slipped to `ཕག་མོ་ནག་མོ` (109.1). Kept, note only: `ཕག་མོ` reads as a name and the sense does not force one reading.
4. 108.5 snake-headed རླུང་ལྷ (two snake heads in the north): kept, note only.
